glossary.def: A filterable string-collection field on each chunk that lists allowed identities, plus a query filter built from the caller's identities. Applied before ranking.
Retrieving more than k candidates so that enough survive a post-filter. The needed factor is about 1 divided by the visible fraction.
The principal under which retrieval runs: the caller (delegated token) or a service account. It decides what the index or source will return.

A permission field type in Azure AI Search native ACLs. It holds a string that names an Azure scope, and a user passes if they hold a qualifying Azure role assignment for it. At most five distinct values per index.
A label on each source (curated, internal, open) that retrieval can filter on, so high-stakes questions use only the most trusted content.
Reconstructing source text, or parts of it, from its embedding vector.
Leaking data in the URL of an image or link the model writes, which the client fetches automatically.
Untrusted content, access to private data and an outbound channel in one session. Together they enable exfiltration.
Group membership through nesting: a user in group A, where A belongs to group B, is also a member of B.
Exposure of the prompt text. The prompt must be treated as public, so no credentials or authorization rules belong in it.

claims.text: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 ids: LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, LLM09 Misinformation, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption.
OWASP LLM01 says RAG and fine-tuning do not fully mitigate prompt injection.

EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711) chained a classifier bypass, reference-style Markdown to evade link redaction, auto-fetched images and an allowed Teams proxy; NVD record published 2025-06-11; CVSS 3.1 base 9.3 (Microsoft) and 7.5 (NVD).
PoisonedRAG reported 90% attack success with five malicious texts per target question in a knowledge base of millions of texts, and found the tested defences insufficient.

MITRE ATLAS ids: AML.T0051.001 Indirect prompt injection, AML.T0064 Gather RAG-Indexed Targets, AML.T0070 RAG Poisoning, AML.T0071 False RAG Entry Injection, AML.T0086 Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation.

OWASP LLM08:2025 lists unauthorized access, cross-context leaks in multi-tenant stores, embedding inversion and data poisoning, and recommends permission-aware stores, data validation, source authentication and immutable retrieval logs.
Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly from embeddings of two models and recovered full names from clinical notes (EMNLP 2023).
OWASP LLM07 says the system prompt should not be considered a secret or a security control, and that the risk is delegating authorization to the model.
OWASP LLM05 advises encoding model output for its context, validating it before passing it downstream and applying strict content security policies.

Azure AI Search vectorFilterMode has preFilter, postFilter and strictPostFilter (preview). preFilter is the default for indexes created after about 2023-10-15, and older indexes default to postFilter and must be recreated to use preFilter.

A security filter uses a Collection(Edm.String) field with filterable true and retrievable false; retrievable false is not field-level security; ACLs can be updated with merge or mergeOrUpload; the pattern does not authenticate callers.
search.in returns sub-second results with hundreds or thousands of values, has no explicit item cap, is limited by the maximum request size, and its latency grows with the number of values.
Maximum indexes per Azure AI Search service: Basic 15, S1 50, S2 200, S3 200, S3 HD 1,000 per partition or 3,000 per service.
Azure AI Search documents three multitenant models: index per tenant, service per tenant, or a mix where large tenants get their own service.

The Azure Architecture Center says store-per-tenant costs more and can hit service limits, multitenant stores need a tenant discriminator and user-level filter on every retrieval including in agent loops, and RLS is not typically used in multitenant designs.
In Azure SQL and SQL Server a shared application login must set the user in SESSION_CONTEXT for row-level security predicates to see the user.
In PostgreSQL, superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass row security and table owners bypass it unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Retrieval API limits: 200 requests per user per hour, queryString 1,500 characters, at most 25 results; pay-as-you-go consumption is a preview.

Native Azure AI Search ACL enforcement uses header x-ms-query-source-authorization, requires Search Index Data Reader (or Contributor) for the caller, passes a document if any of userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches, resolves nested groups through Microsoft Graph and fails closed with a 5xx if Graph is unavailable.

Native ACL schema: permissionFilterOption enabled; at most one field per permission type; 1,000 values per userIds or groupIds field; at most five distinct rbacScope values per index; Entra object ids; special values all and none.

From 2025-11-01-preview ACL filters apply even with an API key or admin role and a missing user token returns only public documents; elevated read uses header x-ms-enable-elevated-read: true on Search POST with REST 2026-05-01-preview or later.
ADLS Gen2 supports up to 32 ACL entries per file or directory and SharePoint up to 1,000 permission entries per file for native ACL enforcement; entries beyond the limit might not be enforced.
An indexed knowledge source created without ingestionPermissionOptions has no permission metadata, so results come back unfiltered regardless of the header.
Azure AI Search latest stable data-plane API is 2026-04-01 and the latest preview is 2026-08-01-preview; native ACL, Purview label and SharePoint ACL features need a preview API.

The SharePoint indexer ACL support (preview) covers inheritance, unique item ACLs, Entra groups, list items, ASPX pages and site groups (spg: prefix) but not Anyone or People in your organization links, guests or Information Management policies, and does not expand an Entra group nested inside a SharePoint group.
From 2026-05-01-preview unique-permission item ACL changes are picked up per indexer run; parent-scope changes need /resync with options ["permissions"] or /resetdocs.

Purview label enforcement in Azure AI Search (preview) needs a system-assigned managed identity, is single-tenant, REST and SDK only, requires the label on every chunk row, and disables Autocomplete and Suggest.
When a Purview label applies encryption, the user needs the EXTRACT usage right as well as VIEW for AI apps to return the content.

The OBO flow uses grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer and requested_token_use on_behalf_of, requires the assertion's audience to be the middle-tier app, uses delegated scopes only and requires the middle tier to surface Conditional Access challenges.
An Entra token carries at most 200 groups for JWT, 150 for SAML and 6 for the implicit flow before an overage indicator replaces the groups claim.
Graph transitiveMemberOf pages at 100 by default and 999 at most, and advanced queries need ConsistencyLevel: eventual, which reads an index that might not reflect recent changes.
Indexer schedule interval is 5 to 1,440 minutes, and push ingestion can update ACL fields immediately with merge.
Graph driveItem change notifications average under one minute with a six-hour maximum, and directory subscriptions last at most 41,760 minutes (under 29 days).
API Management llm-semantic-cache-lookup uses score-threshold from 0.0 to 1.0 (lower is stricter, start near 0.05, above 0.2 may mismatch) and vary-by to partition the cache by user or group id.

Provider prompt caches: OpenAI not shared across organizations; Azure OpenAI not shared between subscriptions; Anthropic isolated per organization and per workspace on the Claude API and Microsoft Foundry.
An ICML 2025 audit found global prompt cache sharing across users in seven API providers at study time, with timing differences that could leak other users' prompts.
Spotlighting has three modes (delimiting, datamarking, encoding) and cut attack success from above 50% to below 2% in the authors' tests on GPT-family models.
Prompt Shields Spotlighting (preview, checked 2026-10-13) is off by default, base64-encodes documents, applies only to models used through Chat Completions and can raise token counts.
CaMeL solved 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security versus 84% undefended.
OWASP LLM06 mitigations: minimise extensions, minimise extension functionality, avoid open-ended extensions, minimise extension permissions.
